step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 42-year-old male with acute febrile jaundice, transaminitis, and subsequent relapsing hepatitis

step5_concept_grounding: Yellow fever virus (YFV) infection confirmed by RT-PCR with clinical hepatitis

evidence_items.source_quote: Upon hepatologist consultation, it was found that the YF-PCR ordered during the first hepatitis episode was positive, thus corroborating the suspicion of relapsing hepatitis due to YF.

A 42-year-old, otherwise healthy, male was admitted to the emergency room with a four-day history of malaise, myalgia, and high-grade fever. Laboratory tests showed increased liver enzymes (aspartate aminotransferase [AST] 2216 U/L and alanine aminotransferase [ALT] 1611 U/L), but normal bilirubin.
evidence_items.test_name: Clinical presentation and hepatic enzyme panel
evidence_items.target_concept: Acute hepatitis due to Yellow fever

rationale: A 42-year-old male was admitted with high-grade fever, malaise, myalgia, severe transaminitis (AST 2216 U/L, ALT 1611 U/L), and subsequent jaundice. Yellow fever virus PCR performed during the acute episode was confirmed positive, establishing acute yellow fever infection and explaining subsequent late-onset hepatitis relapse. E1 confirmatory lab evidence is present for the primary human patient in the current episode. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Single patient from Sao Bernardo do Campo admitted with acute arboviral illness

step5_concept_grounding: Yellow fever virus (YFV) detected alongside dengue 2 virus via multiplex molecular assay

evidence_items.source_quote: In multiplex qRT-PCR, genetic material from DENV2 and YFV was detected.
Rapid antibody tests for dengue (IgM and IgG) and viral protein NS1 were negative, while the test for YFV IgM was inconclusive.
evidence_items.test_name: Rapid antibody test for YFV IgM

rationale: A patient presented in July 2018 with acute symptoms of fever, myalgia, and headache during co-circulation of arboviruses in Brazil. Serum multiplex qRT-PCR definitively detected genetic material of both yellow fever virus (YFV) and dengue serotype 2 (DENV2), confirming a true coinfection. Inconclusive rapid IgM testing does not contradict the confirmatory E1 molecular result. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 13-year-old boy evaluated and diagnosed with narcolepsy type 1 with cataplexy

step5_concept_grounding: Yellow fever is referenced solely as prior vaccination with Stamaril live attenuated vaccine

evidence_items.source_quote: He never received the Pandemrix influenza vaccine, but ~2 weeks prior to symptom onset had been vaccinated with the Stamaril live, attenuated yellow fever vaccine for a family trip to Africa.

rationale: A 13-year-old boy presented with cataplexy and daytime sleepiness, and was diagnosed with narcolepsy type 1. Yellow fever appears exclusively as historical receipt of the Stamaril live, attenuated yellow fever vaccine ~2 weeks prior to symptom onset, explored as a hypothetical autoimmune trigger via molecular mimicry. The patient had no active or confirmed yellow fever infection. Per protocol, vaccination context cannot establish an infection claim. VPD = false -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 65-year-old unvaccinated male traveler presenting with acute yellow fever

step5_concept_grounding: Yellow fever virus (YFV) infection confirmed by molecular detection, serology, and viral isolation

evidence_items.source_quote: However, a urine sample obtained 10 days after initial symptoms was positive for YFV RNA (cycle threshold [Ct] 17.42, 9.3 x 106 RNA copies/mL) by qRT-PCR. We also performed a qualitative IgM-capture ELISA with a specific virus antigen and obtained positive results (optical density 1.19).
evidence_items.target_concept: Yellow fever virus RNA and IgM

evidence_items.source_quote: We isolated YFV in cell culture, which confirmed virus integrity. We also confirmed infectivity after a second virus passage (Ct 24.35, 6.7 x 104 RNA copies/mL).
evidence_items.test_name: Yellow fever virus isolation in cell culture

rationale: A 65-year-old unvaccinated male presented with acute febrile illness, ecchymosis, and thrombocytopenia after traveling to an endemic area in Minas Gerais, Brazil. Yellow fever virus was definitively confirmed by specific qRT-PCR in urine (Ct 17.42) and semen, positive IgM-capture ELISA, viral isolation in cell culture, and whole-genome sequencing (BRMG-2017 strain). E1 confirmatory lab criteria are fully satisfied. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 21-year-old female traveler from Luanda, Angola, evaluated for high fever

step5_concept_grounding: Yellow fever virus evaluated as differential diagnosis during ongoing outbreak in Angola and ruled out

evidence_items.source_quote: Although the patient was supposedly vaccinated against yellow fever virus, we performed real-time reverse transcription PCR for yellow fever virus, and the result was confirmed to be negative.
evidence_items.test_name: real-time reverse transcription PCR for yellow fever virus

evidence_items.source_quote: Testing for other arboviruses was performed, and real-time reverse transcription PCR for chikungunya virus (CHIKV) showed a positive result. Therefore, the final diagnosis was chikungunya fever.
evidence_items.test_name: real-time reverse transcription PCR for chikungunya virus

rationale: A 21-year-old female traveler from Luanda, Angola, presented to a hospital in Tokyo with high fever during an ongoing yellow fever outbreak in Angola. Yellow fever virus real-time reverse transcription PCR was performed to evaluate the differential diagnosis and was confirmed negative. An alternative pathogen (chikungunya virus) was detected by RT-PCR, establishing chikungunya fever as the definitive diagnosis. Target disease was explicitly tested and ruled out. VPD = false -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 67-year-old woman presenting with status epilepticus and diagnosed with YEL-AND

step5_concept_grounding: Yellow fever vaccine-associated neurotropic disease (YEL-AND) resulting from 17D live attenuated vaccine

evidence_items.source_quote: Two months prior to presentation, she received CDC recommended vaccinations in anticipation of traveling to Guyana, South America, which included the 17D yellow fever virus (YFV) and Hepatitis B vaccines.
CSF YFV IgM positivity with titer levels close to those in serum confirmed a diagnosis of YEL-AND.
evidence_items.test_name: CSF and serum YFV IgM and PRNT90

rationale: A 67-year-old woman developed status epilepticus and encephalopathy following receipt of the 17D yellow fever vaccine, with CSF and serum YFV IgM and PRNT90 confirming yellow fever vaccine-associated neurotropic disease (YEL-AND). The MultiCaRe protocol explicitly establishes that vaccine-associated adverse events are categorized under clinical_role = PREVENTION_VACCINATION and do not represent wild-type yellow fever infection. Because wild-type infection is not present, VPD = false -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 50-year-old woman presenting with diffuse uveitis and chorioretinal changes after YF vaccination

step5_concept_grounding: Yellow fever mention reflects immunization and subsequent vaccine-associated adverse event

evidence_items.source_quote: A 50-year-old caucasian Brazilian woman with no previous ocular or systemic diseases received one dose of YF vaccine in April 2017 (Biomanguinhos/Fiocruz, lot 160VFA0433, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil).
Bilateral asymmetric diffuse uveitis was diagnosed and oral prednisone (40 mg/daily) was started.

rationale: A 50-year-old female received a single dose of yellow fever vaccine and developed fever, thrombocytopenia, and acute kidney injury followed by bilateral diffuse uveitis. The clinical narrative describes a vaccine-related adverse event with clinical_role = PREVENTION_VACCINATION rather than wild-type yellow fever infection. Per protocol rules, vaccine adverse events do not represent a valid clinical claim for target disease infection. VPD = false -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 10-month-old female infant presenting with fatal vaccine-associated viscerotropic/neurotropic disease revealing SCID

step5_concept_grounding: Vaccine-associated viscerotropic and neurotropic disease from 17DD yellow fever live attenuated vaccine

evidence_items.source_quote: The mother reported that, 28 days before the onset of symptoms, the child had received yellow fever vaccine (17DD) produced by the Immunobiological Technology Institute (Bio-Manguinhos - Fiocruz).

The possibility of vaccine-associated viscerotropic and neurotropic disease was considered by the infectious disease team since the onset of symptoms followed the first dose of YFV. The patient was tested for antibodies against the yellow fever virus (MAC-ELISA) on serum and CSF samples, showing positive IgM results.
evidence_items.test_name: MAC-ELISA for yellow fever virus antibodies
evidence_items.target_concept: Yellow fever vaccine-associated viscerotropic and neurotropic disease

rationale: A 10-month-old infant developed severe viscerotropic and neurotropic disease 28 days after receiving the 17DD yellow fever live vaccine, leading to the clinical identification of severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) and eventual death. The disease presentation was a catastrophic adverse event caused by the attenuated vaccine strain in an immunocompromised host, classified under clinical_role = PREVENTION_VACCINATION. It does not represent community-acquired wild-type yellow fever infection. Under project criteria, vaccine adverse events cannot produce an affirmed target infection claim. VPD = false -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.
